newsitem.title: JAPAN: TIFFE Euroyen ends firmer, overnight rate surges.
newsitem.headline: TIFFE Euroyen ends firmer, overnight rate surges.

text.p: Key three-month Euroyen deposit rate futures closed Monday firmer, underpinned by falls in Tokyo stocks on the last day of the 1996/97 financial year.
The Nikkei stock average ended down 186.32 at 18,003.40 after clawing back above the key 18,000 level toward the close.
The key overnight call rate surged to the highest levels since the Bank of Japan's (BOJ) last rate cut in 1995 due to banks' strong demand for funds covering the business year-end.
The key overnight rate was mostly traded at and above 0.70 percent on Monday against Friday's weighted average of 0.51.

The rate briefly rose as high as 0.85 percent this afternoon, the highest rate since September 1995 when the BOJ cut the discount rate to 0.5 percent and started guiding the key overnight rate slightly below the discount rate on average.
The rate was boosted by some banks which were in great need of overnight money after failing to raise enough long-term funds covering the fiscal year-end, traders said.
"The overnight rate surged higher than what many had expected of around 0.60 percent," said a city bank dealer.

He said that was partly because financial institutions that received government payments this morning and were expected to supply funds to the market had been hesitant to do so until after 3 p.m. (0600 GMT) when they had a better idea of their own needs for the year-end.

The BOJ conducted a more accommodative operation than expected at 0020 GMT and supplied an extra 100 billion yen at 0222 GMT. As a result, the market was in net surplus of an estimated 400 billion yen for the day.
But banks' seasonally strong fund-raising demands kept the key overnight rate from falling sharply, traders said.
Offering rates of longer-term money rates firmed in line with a jump at the short-end of the market. But no trade was detected in one-, two- or three-month certificates of deposit.
The key December three-month Euroyen deposit rate futures contract ended up 0.02 at 99.05. It moved between 99.03 and 99.05 in turnover of 14,009 contracts.
Major banks were sidelined ahead of a shift in their accounting method to one based on market prices on April 1.
Activity was thin also ahead of the release of the BOJ's "tankan" corporate survey on April 2, traders said.
